notes:
Here are three solid options for a preschooler visiting New York City September 12–15:

**1. Children's Museum of Manhattan (Upper West Side)**

NYC's premier children's museum for ages 0–6 in the Upper West Side!
 
During July–September, the museum runs Monday – Sunday, 10 am – 5 pm.
 That covers every day of a Sept 12–15 stay. The site did not post a standard adult/child ticket price in what I found — it mentions discounted admission programs (Cool Culture, Museums for All) but not the regular rate, so you'd want to check at the door or call ahead.

**2. Central Park Zoo (Midtown)**
A compact, stroller-friendly zoo well suited to young kids. 
From April 2 through October 31, 2026, the zoo is open Mon-Fri 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM, and weekends & federal holidays 10:00 AM - 5:30 PM, with last entry one hour before closing.
 
Admission rates are Adult (13 & over) $22.95/$15.95, Senior (65 & over) $18.95/$12.95, Child (3-12) $16.95/$9.95, and Child (2 & under) free
 (first figure is the full "Total Experience" ticket with 4-D theater, second is the "Limited Admission" option).

**3. New York Aquarium (Coney Island, Brooklyn)**
Worth the trip if you have a full day — pair it with the boardwalk. 
From September 8 – October 31, 2026 the aquarium opens daily at 10:00am, with last entry at 4:00pm and closing at 5:00pm
, so it's running on this exact window. 
Admission is Adult $29.95 off-peak/$32.95 peak, Senior $27.95/$29.95, Child (3-12) $25.95/$27.95, and Child (2 & under) is free
.

A few honest notes: the Children's Museum's current ticket price wasn't listed on the pages I could read, and several sites quoting "aquarium hours" disagreed slightly, so I went with the aquarium's own hours-and-rates page as the most current. All three are indoor/outdoor-friendly for a preschooler and close enough together (Manhattan + Brooklyn) to combine over a few days.
